summary: There is no line to mutate: no production logic and no test logic changed. The only src/main edit is SubscriptionEvent's javadoc; the only test edit is a class javadoc and one .as() description string -- every assertion predicate is byte-identical, so nothing was weakened. I re-measured the falsifiability claim the record leans on rather than accepting it: discarding the decoded range in SubscriptionEvent.decode (byteStart=byteLen=RANGE_ABSENT after the uvarints) reds exactly 3 of 281 format cases -- aRangeStartingAtBYTEZEROIsNotMistakenForABSENT and aV3EventSurvivesAROUNDTrip in SubscriptionEventGrantTest, aV3DIRECTEventWithARangeMatchesItsGoldenBytes in GoldenSubscriptionEventTest -- and :format:test is green with the mutation reverted. The price claim checks out at the source: subscription-event-direct-v3.bin is 128 bytes, -whole.bin is 123, delta 5, and the ADR correctly separates that fixture's 5 varint bytes from the 7-byte modelled shape it prices on. Both round-2 majors are closed at the wording level. Two are not closed at the level below. Criterion 3's 'FOUR sites' enumeration is ALREADY STALE against these staged bytes -- this commit adds three more banners carrying the identical 'no reader in the tree consumes them' / 'no range is expressible' claim, and a banner WINS over the prose it corrects, which is what round 1 of this task blocked on. And criterion 2 now pins WHAT is counted and WHERE, but not that every request the direct path makes passes through the thing counting: a seam that grows a directory fetch alongside the range fetch shows 1 counted request at both shares while production issues 401, which is the same number my round-2 finding named, relocated out of the counter rather than removed.

findings.title: Criterion 3 enumerates FOUR sites; this same commit creates three more banners carrying the identical claim, and a banner wins over the prose it corrects
findings.failure_scenario: Criterion 3 reads 'whichever way it goes, FOUR sites are corrected, not two: SubscriptionEvent's javadoc and ADR-0044's Decision (b), which both currently say "no reader consumes this"; research doc 04 2c's banner; and SubscriptionEventGrantTest's class javadoc'. Grepped against the staged bytes, the claim 'no reader consumes them' now lives at SEVEN sites, not four, and three of the new ones were added by this very commit: doc 10 8's banner at :220 -- 'The subscription event's byteStart/byteLen are used by **no reader in the tree**'; doc 13 4's banner at :107 -- '**no reader in the tree consumes them**'; doc 10 7's banner at :183-191 -- 'A consumer cannot express a range at all today ... **M5.66** owns making ranges expressible, or removing the coordinates'; plus ADR-0043's new Status block at :3-11, which states 'no range is expressible' and 'The fields stay' as settled. Surviving path, with every word of all four criteria satisfied: M5.66's owner builds the bounded reader, measures the crossover into ADR-0044 (criterion 1), asserts bytes and requests at both shares (criterion 2), corrects exactly the four enumerated sites (criterion 3), scopes the grant to the now-expressible range and updates security.md (criterion 4), marks the row done -- and three RESEARCH BANNERS still tell the next reader that no reader consumes the fields and that a ranged read is not expressible. AGENTS.md states that when an early conclusion and a revision banner disagree, the banner wins, and the `research` skill routes readers to exactly these pages; the round-1 BLOCKING finding on this task was a stale banner in doc 04 2c for precisely this reason, and the sweep table at ADR-0044:245 records that a reader routed there 'would have implemented it'. The list is a hand enumeration -- gate-design rung 7 -- while the artifact that would maintain itself already exists one file away: ADR-0044's sweep table, which has a row for every one of these sites. The fix is to make criterion 3 read on the table rather than on a count ('every row of ADR-0044's sweep table dispositioned Kept or Corrected is re-dispositioned in the same commit, and the table is the list'), which is rung 4 and cannot go stale the next time a banner is added.

findings.location: docs/internal/product/backlog.md:126 (M5.66 criterion 2, 'counted at M5.45g's byte source')
findings.title: The criterion pins where the count is taken, not that every request in the direct path passes through it -- a directory fetch outside the counted method restores the 401
findings.failure_scenario: M5.45g's seam is specified as 'an interface in client taking a Grant and yielding a segment's bytes' -- no range, by this ADR's own decision. A bounded read therefore CANNOT be expressed through that seam as it exists, so M5.66 must widen it, and the criterion pins the count to a seam whose shape the row necessarily changes without saying what is counted afterwards. Surviving implementation: the seam gains fetchRange(Grant, long, long) and fetchDirectory(Grant); the counting test implementation counts fetchRange, which is 'the byte source' in the criterion's sense -- the thing that yields the run's bytes. Favourable share (one run of 1,600): 1 counted request, ~5.2 KiB counted, strictly fewer bytes -- green. Unfavourable share (~400 runs): falls back above the crossover, 1 counted whole-object request -- green. In production the directory fetch runs once per DELIVERY, because nothing holds a segment's directory across the ~400 independent readNext calls: per-node residency is M5.45h's and this row is 'todo -- no dependency; it is a format question', so it may land first, exactly as its own cell argues about M5.45h's K=64 case. That is 400 directory GETs plus one, runs-per-node, forbidden by non-negotiable 6 by name -- the same 401 my round-2 finding measured, moved out of the counter rather than out of the design. Closing it is two clauses: 'every call on the seam is counted, whatever methods it grows -- a directory read is a request' and 'the count asserted is the TOTAL per (node, segment)'. Without them the criterion constrains the instrument's location and not its completeness, and an instrument that misses the request being argued about is the bytes-only defect one layer down.

findings.location: docs/internal/product/backlog.md:126 (M5.66 criterion 2, 'AT THE UNFAVOURABLE SHARE AS WELL AS THE FAVOURABLE ONE')
findings.title: The two-share clause names the quantities but no relation, and 'fewer bytes' cannot hold at the unfavourable share for any correct implementation
findings.failure_scenario: The criterion says the assertion is on bytes fetched AND requests made, both, at both shares. It never says what must be TRUE of either number at the unfavourable share. Read one way it demands 'FEWER BYTES ACTUALLY FETCHED' there too, which no correct implementation can satisfy -- above the crossover the right answer is the same whole-object GET, so bytes are equal, not fewer, and the criterion forbids the correct code. Read the other way it demands only that an assertion mentioning those quantities exists, which assertThat(requests).isPositive() and assertThat(bytes).isPositive() satisfy at K=400 while constraining nothing. Either reading is defective, and the fix is one sentence naming the baseline and the direction per share: at the favourable share strictly fewer bytes and at most 2 requests; at the unfavourable share bytes and requests no worse than the whole-object path's 8 MiB and 1 request per (node, segment).

findings.title: The measured crossover is recorded in the ADR and nothing binds the implementation to it
findings.failure_scenario: Criterion 1 requires the crossover be MEASURED and RECORDED IN ADR-0044 ITSELF. Criterion 2 exercises exactly two shares, 1-of-1,600 and ~400-of-1,600. Nothing requires the number the ADR records to be the number the code branches on, and no case reads both. Surviving implementation: measure and record 'the crossover is at a 2.5% node share (K=40)', then ship 'if (runsHeld <= 1) boundedRead else wholeObject'. K=1 takes the bounded path and shows fewer bytes; K=400 takes the whole-object path and shows 1 request; both criterion-2 arms green, criterion 1 green because the number is in the record. Every node holding 2 to 40 runs then runs the policy the ADR says loses, and the recorded number is decorative -- the recorded-here, implemented-there shape this milestone has corrected five times. Closing it costs one clause: the threshold the code branches on IS the recorded constant, with cases at crossover-1 and crossover+1 deriving their input from it.

findings.title: The javadoc attributes 5.5% to a subtraction that does not produce it
findings.failure_scenario: The field javadoc reads 'priced carrying them at **5.5% of an event** that carries one -- measured from the golden files, 128 bytes against 123'. A reader who does the subtraction the sentence names gets 128 - 123 = 5 and 5/128 = 3.9%, or 6/128 = 4.7% counting the presence byte the fixture pays either way. The 5.5% numerator is 7, and 7 comes from the MODELLED 8 MiB / 1,600-run shape (4 uvarint bytes for byteStart + 2 for byteLen + 1 flag), which this sentence does not mention; the golden files supply the denominator only. ADR-0044:92-107 gets this right and spells out all three numbers -- 5 for the fixture's varints, 6 to remove them from the fixture, 7 at the modelled shape -- and the backlog M5.45f cell also carries 'a MEASURED 7 bytes per event'. The javadoc is the one place chosen because 'a reader looks' there, and it is the one place the derivation cannot be reproduced. One clause fixes it: '7 bytes at the 8 MiB / 1,600-run shape against a 128-byte event measured from the golden files'.

findings.title: The printed consistency check does not reproduce, and the two places the decision is actually argued quote the figure the record says not to decide on
findings.failure_scenario: Line 110-111 prints '0.13 / 2.44 = 5.5%' as the check the earlier pair failed. 0.13 / 2.44 is 5.33%, not 5.5%; the figure is right from the unrounded values (11,200 / 204,800 = 5.47%) and the printed division is not, which is a check that fails its own re-run. Separately, line 111 states 'THE DECISION IS TAKEN ON THE LARGER FIGURE', and then the two places where the decision is actually argued quote only the smaller: alternative (b1) at :174 -- the record's own 'closest call' -- rejects removal because 'at **0.13%** of the segment they describe, keeping them is close to free', Consequences at :208 says 'at a cost of 0.13%', and ADR-0043's new Status block at :6 tells every future reader the price is '0.13% of the segment'. A reader arriving at the closest call therefore never meets the number the record says the call was made on. Both are one-clause fixes and neither changes the outcome, which is why this is minor rather than major.

findings.location: docs/internal/product/backlog.md:126 (M5.66 criterion 4, 'security.md is updated or cited'), against docs/internal/standards/security.md:12-13
findings.title: The weak arm of criterion 4 is the state that already exists, and the pointer only runs one way
findings.failure_scenario: Criterion 4 now names the rule and the standard, which closes my round-2 finding. What it leaves is the discharge: 'Either way security.md is updated or CITED, and not left pointing here.' Citing security.md from an ADR is what ADR-0041, ADR-0043 and ADR-0044 all already did while the clause stayed open for four rows. security.md:13 today reads 'scoped to one key and where possible one range' with no pointer to any of them, so an auditor starting where a security pass starts -- at the standard -- cannot learn that 'possible' was evaluated and answered, nor find M5.66. Four places now point AT M5.66 and nothing points from the standard to anything. If M5.66 takes the decline arm and satisfies criterion 4 by 'citing', rule 3 is unchanged, unqualified, and the question is open for a fifth reader. Dropping 'or cited' -- security.md rule 3 itself carries the answer or a pointer to the record holding it -- is the whole fix.
